intent: To justify the proposal for taxing capital gains by demonstrating that a large majority of Americans believe wealthy individuals are not paying their fair share of taxes.

units.meaning: 80% of Americans are bothered that wealthy people do not pay their fair share, the central majority statistic.

basis.note: Main donut_34 slice value; intent/narration maps it to the fair-share belief.

accepted_routes: 80% believe wealthy people don't pay their fair share
About 80% are bothered by wealthy people not paying their fair share
Four in five Americans hold this view
A large majority (80%) say wealthy people don't pay their fair share
units.visual_evidence_rule: The donut chart must have a dominant 80% slice clearly labeled and tied to the fair-share belief.
units.temporal_anchor: Most Americans are bothered that wealthy people don't pay their fair share
units.reviewer_question: Must the video show 80% as the primary statistic for the fair-share belief?

units.meaning: The complement or remainder of the donut is 20%.
accepted_routes: 20% is the remaining share
The rest of the donut is 20%
A 20% remainder complements the 80% slice
One in five is outside the majority category
units.visual_evidence_rule: The 20% remainder slice is visible and labeled if the full donut composition is shown.
units.temporal_anchor: No separate narration clause; can appear as chart context during the fair-share sentence.
units.reviewer_question: Is showing or labeling the 20% remainder required, or is it optional chart completeness?

units.meaning: The 80% share should be framed as a large majority or as exceeding the majority threshold.

basis.note: Majority framing comes from intent/narration; the table supplies the 80% share.

accepted_routes: 80% is a large majority
The majority view is 80%
80% is well above a simple majority
Most Americans—80%—hold this view
units.visual_evidence_rule: Annotation or narration must explicitly call the 80% slice a majority or large majority, not just present a bare number.
units.temporal_anchor: Most Americans are bothered that wealthy people don't pay their fair share
units.reviewer_question: Should the video explicitly mark 80% as a large majority threshold, rather than leaving the inference to the viewer?

units.meaning: The donut's two segments compose the whole at 80% plus 20% equals 100%.
accepted_routes: The chart splits into 80% and 20%
80% plus a 20% remainder make the full donut
The composition is 80% versus 20% of the total
The two shares sum to 100% (80% + 20%)
units.visual_evidence_rule: Both slices are shown with their labels so the donut visually sums to a complete whole.
units.temporal_anchor: Can accompany the fair-share sentence as chart composition.
units.reviewer_question: Must the video show the complete 80/20 composition, or is the 80% slice alone sufficient?

units.meaning: The 80% share is four times the 20% remainder.
accepted_routes: 80% is four times 20%
The majority share is 4x the remainder
For every 20% remainder, there is 80% main share
80% versus 20% is a 4-to-1 split
units.visual_evidence_rule: Either slice sizes or an annotation should make the 4-to-1 ratio visible.
units.temporal_anchor: The fair-share sentence, as a supporting comparison.
units.reviewer_question: Should the video quantify the 80/20 gap as 4-to-1, or only show the slices?

optional_valid: Use color emphasis to distinguish the 80% majority slice from the 20% remainder.
A 20% remainder label can be shown without labeling what that group believes.
unsupported_to_avoid: Causal claim that capital gains taxes would fix unfairness or be an easy solution
Claim that 80% support capital gains tax specifically
Claim that the 20% remainder opposes capital gains taxes
Claim about wealthy individuals' actual tax rates or dollars paid
Extrapolation beyond the two table values 80 and 20
notes: Core required content is the 80% fair-share majority; 20%, composition, and the 4x ratio are defensible optional support. Avoid attaching unsupported policy causality to the donut.
file_naming: one G1 per input contract; B1/B3/B4/B5 need separate drafts
narration_use: reference only when drafting; required units must be derivable from the public B2 inputs (table + intent)
weight_mode_note: every unit gets 1/n so coverage is a plain share; weight_template is kept for per-type analysis only
